chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'There is no servant whom I intend to admit to Paradise except that I afflict him in his body. If that is an expiation for his sins, or else I intensify [the affliction] upon him at his death until he comes to Me with no sin, then I admit him to Paradise.'

And there is no servant whom I intend to admit to the Fire except that I make his body sound. If that is completion of his request for Me, or else I secure his fear from his ruler. If that is completion of his request for Me, or else I expand his sustenance for him. If that is completion of his request for Me, or else I ease his death for him until he comes to Me with no good deed for Me, then I admit him to the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind God afflicting believers with illness or granting ease to disbelievers?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi from Al-Kafi elucidates the concept of *Tadhyil* (hastening punishment) and *Tas'ir* (delaying punishment) in the Hereafter, illustrating how worldly conditions serve as divine mechanisms for spiritual accounting. Shia scholars emphasize that for the elect, physical trials act as expiation (*Kaffarah*) for minor sins, while for the condemned, worldly ease and security ensure they receive a fair trial (*Adl*) before entering Hell, leaving no excuse of hardship. The text highlights the precision of Divine Justice, where every aspect of life, from health to sustenance, is calibrated to either purify the believer or complete the record of the disbeliever.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “There is none from a servant that I<sup>azwj</sup> Intend to Enter him into the Paradise except that I<sup>azwj</sup> Afflict him (by an illness) in his body. So if it was that, it would be an expiation for his sins, or else I<sup>azwj</sup> would Intensify (the pangs) upon him during his death until he comes to Me<sup>azwj</sup> and there would be no sin for him, then I<sup>azwj</sup> would Enter him into the Paradise.

And there is none from a servant that I<sup>azwj</sup> Intend to Enter him into the Fire except that I<sup>azwj</sup> would Grant good health for him in his body. So if it was that, it would complete what he is seeking for in My<sup>azwj</sup> Presence, or else I<sup>azwj</sup> would Grant security for his fear from his ruling authority. So if it was that, it would complete what his is seeking for in My<sup>azwj</sup> Presence, or else I<sup>azwj</sup> would Expand his sustenance upon him. So if it was that, it would complete what he is seeking for in My<sup>azwj</sup> Presence, or else I<sup>azwj</sup> would Ease his death upon him until he comes to me and there would be not good deed for him in My<sup>azwj</sup> Prsence, then I<sup>azwj</sup> would Enter him into the Hell’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu’awiyah ibn Wahab from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, “Any servant whom I want to admit in paradise I cause bodily suffering to expiate for his sins, if this would not be enough I then cause dying to become a severe suffering until he comes before Me without any sins, then I admit him in paradise. “Any servant whom I want to go in fire, I grant him health in his body. If this completes compensation to him I then call him to My presence, otherwise, I grant him security from the rulers. If this completes compensation to him I then call him in My presence, otherwise, I expand the means for his living. If this completes compensation to him I then call him in My presence, otherwise, I make dying easy for him so he comes in My presence without any good deeds before Me, then I send him in fire.’”
